title: Two Hundred Feet of Willis
hook: The corner is gone. Four driveways. Insulin, none.
scene: The corner is gone too — a transformer came down across it in the night and the wires are still on the pole. No block to drive. Four driveways in reach: one across the street, one thirty feet up on your side against a blind hedge, one on your side with clean sight down Willis, one behind you past the crest. Insulin, none.
decision: No block. You are backing into a driveway. Which one?

options.text: Your side, the one with clear sight down Willis — signal, check behind, back in
options.result: You pull just past it, blinker on, nothing behind you, and reverse in with two hundred feet of empty road in the mirror the whole time. Shift to drive, check both ways, and roll out pointed the right direction.

options.text: The one across the street — it is the widest and the apron is flat
options.result: Backing into it means dragging the car across the oncoming lane and sitting in it, sideways, blind to the crest. The apron is flat and it does not matter. You are a gate across the only road.

options.text: The near one at thirty feet — closest, least time exposed
options.result: The hedge eats Willis at about eighty feet. You are in reverse with a sightline shorter than your stopping distance, and the first thing you would know about anything coming is the sound of it.

options.text: Past the crest behind you — the driveway there is long and straight
options.result: You reverse up and over the crest to reach it, which means backing blind over the one piece of road you cannot see the far side of. The driveway is fine. Everything before the driveway is not.

debrief: A two-point turn backs into a driveway on the same side of the street as your car, at a spot with at least two hundred feet of visible oncoming road. Pull just past it, signal, confirm nothing is behind you, then reverse. Shift to drive and check both directions before you pull out.

source.teaching_target: Two-point turn: same-side driveway, 200 feet of visible oncoming traffic, signal, confirm clear behind, back in, then check both directions before pulling out.

image_brief.subject: high overhead of Willis: the faded matte-pink Baja VW Beetle in the right-hand lane, rear mesh nearer the camera, wide flat plow pointing at a dead corner; four driveway aprons in reach
image_brief.foreground: a long empty stretch of wet residential street behind the Beetle, a paved driveway on the RIGHT curb with clean sight down that stretch; a low crest further behind with a fourth driveway past it
image_brief.midground: on the RIGHT curb about thirty feet toward the corner, a driveway eaten by a tall live hedge; on the LEFT curb, a wide flat driveway across the street
image_brief.background: the corner ahead is blocked — a fallen transformer and slack wires on the pole, no through-road, Kent houses, bare maples, flat gray morning
image_brief.read: the same-side open apron has two hundred feet of empty Willis; the hedge apron, the far-side apron, and the crest apron do not

geometry.ego_nose_in_frame: the plow blade points toward the blocked corner at the top of the frame
